title: An automated equity-research desk
context: Personal research system — nights and weekends
summary: To learn institutional research discipline properly, I built the whole stack: role-based AI agents (analyst, PM, risk, macro, scout) write dated research memos on a schedule, a valuation engine runs DCF and comparables on every name, and market data is grounded in WRDS — Wharton's institutional research database — with cross-source integrity checks.
highlights: 7 role-based agent workflows produce dated, filed research memos — holding briefs, weekly PM reviews, risk reports, macro briefings, idea scouting
DCF + comparables valuation engine computes fair value for every covered name
WRDS institutional data backfill with cross-source integrity checks against market feeds
Lookahead-safe backtester with walk-forward out-of-sample validation and crisis stress-testing
Daily news and macro briefs generate automatically via CI; the terminal self-deploys on every push
impact: A student teaching himself institutional research discipline by building the entire stack — data, valuation, memos, and review cadence.

title: Worker Master — running a real agency on AI ops
context: Smile Employment Agency — my own licensed company
summary: The operations platform behind my employment agency: a spreadsheet-backed workforce system with a mobile app, per-company quota calculators, and AI-driven compliance audits — supporting 50+ work-pass placements and 20+ corporate clients.
highlights: Google Sheets as the system of record, with a mobile web app for viewing and editing worker records from anywhere, 24/7 on a self-hosted server
Per-company work-pass quota calculator built into the companies view
AI compliance suite: bilingual (中文/English) audit workbooks, cross-shop double-submission detection, and an email-scanning blacklist of workers flagged by regulators
Hourly two-way sync between the cloud sheet and local mirrors, with a health watchdog
impact: One founder runs compliance-heavy manpower operations that normally need a back-office team.

title: The Post Room — an AI inbox concierge
context: Email + learning system over two Gmail accounts
summary: A dependency-free Python server plus headless LLM workers that read two Gmail accounts and produce a daily morning brief: grouped newsletter digests, extracted deadlines, and a finance-news desk with a spaced-repetition concept ledger that turns reading into retained knowledge.
highlights: Custom multi-account Gmail MCP server (read-only OAuth) shared by every feature
Each smart feature is a small module that shells out to a headless LLM and caches JSON — no database, no framework, no paid API
Finance Desk turns newsletter flow into a regime board, running threads, and a glossary with spaced-repetition review
Daily 7am rebuild emails the brief automatically; deadline extraction catches school, billing, and reply-by dates
impact: Two overflowing inboxes became one five-minute morning brief that also compounds finance knowledge.

title: Telegram concierge & mission-control board
summary: A Telegram bot that grew into a personal operations hub: expense tracking with receipt OCR, bank-statement parsing, and a worker-edit queue for my agency — audited by a mission-control dashboard that health-checks every feature.
highlights: Natural-language expense logging with OCR receipt reading and bank-statement intake, backed by Google Sheets
14+ live features tracked on a mission-control board with real-time status pills and one-click tests per feature
A 'build a feature' button that opens a seeded AI coding session pointed at the bot's repo — the bot helps build itself
Runs 24/7 on a self-hosted server as a systemd service
impact: A single chat thread replaces an expense app, a document parser, and an ops queue.

title: Idea Scout & automated research pipelines
summary: A weekly multi-source scout that scans GitHub, Hacker News, Reddit, and YouTube, scores every candidate against a written interests profile, and publishes a ranked digest — alongside a deep-research harness that fans out parallel agents to produce cited, fact-checked reports.
highlights: Multi-source ingestion with per-source adapters (including an RSS workaround for bot-blocked platforms)
Scoring driven by a plain-markdown interests file — editing the profile retunes the scout with zero code changes
Deep-research harness: parallel search agents, adversarial claim verification, synthesized cited reports
Keeper research publishes to a personal learnings dashboard with spaced-repetition review
impact: A standing research department for one person, on a student budget of $0.

title: The Desk — a personal cloud of ~60 agents
context: The umbrella system tying everything together
summary: Every system I build ships to one self-hosted hub: a dashboard of dashboards with a registry of ~60 agents and scheduled automations, health watchdogs driving live status lights, 30+ custom AI skills, and usage telemetry.
highlights: Agent registry tracking ~60 live agents and scheduled jobs across all projects
A watchdog timer health-checks every service and drives status lights on the hub
30+ custom skills — from compliance audits to options-trading tutors — invocable from any AI session
Two-way file sync lets me edit any project's context files from my phone; token-usage telemetry on its own dashboard
impact: The proof of breadth: one student operating infrastructure that behaves like a small company's internal tooling.

title: House Finder — an autonomous housing agent
context: Finding my own exchange-semester flat in Dublin
summary: An end-to-end autonomous agent for a real personal problem: it scans Dublin housing sources, scores fit against my constraints, sends enquiries as me by email and browser form-fill, and answers landlord replies with an LLM reply-brain — escalating only high-stakes messages for one-click approval.
highlights: 100+ enquiries sent autonomously: direct agent emails plus browser-automated listing-site forms
Reply-brain classifies inbound landlord replies; low-stakes responses send fully automatically, risky ones queue in an approval dashboard
Hard safety rails: never books, pays, signs, or re-contacts; money/commitment topics always escalate
Recurring pipeline: daily source refresh, 20-minute reply loop, synced read-only mirror
impact: A months-long housing search runs itself in the background while I study.
